name: Seiko
tagline: Japan's watchmaking giant, from the first quartz watch to cult-favorite divers
summary: Seiko is Japan's most famous watch brand and one of the few truly vertically integrated manufacturers in the world, making everything from hairsprings to quartz crystals in-house. It changed the industry forever with the 1969 Astron, the world's first quartz wristwatch, and remains a benchmark for value-driven mechanical watches.
history:
Seiko traces its roots to 1881, when 21-year-old Kintaro Hattori opened a watch and clock shop, K. Hattori, in Tokyo's Ginza district. In 1892 he founded the Seikosha factory to produce wall clocks, and in 1913 it made the Laurel, Japan's first wristwatch. The Great Kanto Earthquake of 1923 destroyed the factory, but Hattori rebuilt, and in 1924 the first watches bearing the Seiko name appeared.

The post-war decades turned Seiko into a technical powerhouse. Internal competition between its Suwa Seikosha and Daini Seikosha factories produced Grand Seiko (1960), King Seiko (1961) and Japan's first diver's watch (1965). Seiko timed the 1964 Tokyo Olympics and, in 1969, launched the Quartz Astron, the world's first quartz wristwatch, along with one of the first automatic chronographs, the 6139.

Quartz technology, which Seiko chose not to lock behind patents, reshaped the global industry and helped trigger the 'quartz crisis' that devastated Swiss watchmaking in the 1970s and 80s. Seiko continued innovating with Kinetic (1988), Spring Drive (1999) and the Astron GPS Solar (2012).

Today Seiko Watch Corporation is part of Seiko Group Corporation, still led by the Hattori family. Its range stretches from the affordable Seiko 5 Sports to Prospex divers, Presage dress watches and Astron, while Grand Seiko was spun off as an independent brand in 2017.

models.name: Prospex 1965 Heritage Diver's (62MAS)
models.description: A modern recreation of the 1965 62MAS, Japan's first diver's watch. The SPB45x generation brought a slimmer case, 300 m rating and 72-hour power reserve.

models.name: Prospex 'Turtle'
models.description: The reissue of Seiko's 1976 cushion-cased 6309 diver, nicknamed 'Turtle' for its shell-like shape. One of the most beloved affordable dive watches ever made.

models.name: 5 Sports SKX Series
models.description: The spiritual successor to the legendary SKX007 and the most popular entry point into mechanical watches for a generation of collectors.

models.name: Presage Cocktail Time

name: Grand Seiko
tagline: Japanese nature, Zaratsu polish and the glide of Spring Drive
summary: Grand Seiko is Seiko's luxury marque, founded in 1960 to create the best watch possible. Known for razor-sharp Zaratsu polishing, nature-inspired dials and the unique Spring Drive movement, it has become the most credible Japanese challenger to Swiss luxury watchmaking.
history:
Grand Seiko was born in 1960 at Seiko's Suwa Seikosha factory with a simple aim: to make a watch as accurate, durable and beautiful as any in the world. The first Grand Seiko, a manually wound watch with a Chronometer-grade movement, was followed by landmark references such as the 44GS of 1967, whose design codified the 'Grand Seiko Style' of flat, mirror-polished surfaces and distortion-free reflections.

The brand thrived until the quartz revolution shifted Seiko's priorities; mechanical Grand Seiko production paused in the mid-1970s. It returned in 1988 with ultra-precise 9F quartz, and in 1998 the mechanical 9S caliber revived the line. In 2004 Spring Drive, a movement combining a mainspring with an electronic regulator and a gliding seconds hand, joined the range.

For decades Grand Seiko was largely sold in Japan. It began international distribution in 2010 and in 2017 became an independent brand, dropping the 'Seiko' name from the dial. Signature pieces like the 'Snowflake' SBGA211 and the 'White Birch' SLGH005 have won global acclaim, the latter taking a prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève in 2021.

Watches are made at the Shizukuishi Watch Studio in Iwate (mechanical) and the Shinshu Watch Studio in Nagano (Spring Drive and quartz). The 2022 Kodo constant-force tourbillon signalled its move into haute horlogerie.
knownFor: Zaratsu polishing, nature-inspired dials and Spring Drive
innovations: 1967: 44GS establishes the 'Grand Seiko Style' design grammar
1968: 61GS, Japan's first 10-beat automatic
1993: 9F quartz with twin-pulse control and instant date change
2004: Spring Drive introduced in Grand Seiko
2020: Cal. 9SA5 with Dual Impulse Escapement
2022: Kodo constant-force tourbillon

funFacts: The 'Snowflake' dial was inspired by snow drifts in the Hotaka mountains visible from the Shinshu studio.
Zaratsu polishing is named after the German Sallaz machine once used for the technique.

models.name: Snowflake
models.description: Grand Seiko's breakout international hit: a textured white dial evoking wind-swept snow, blued seconds hand and a light titanium case.

models.name: White Birch
models.description: The Evolution 9 flagship with a deeply textured silver dial recalling white birch forests, powered by the 36,000 vph 9SA5. GPHG prize winner 2021.

models.name: Shunbun (62GS reinterpretation)
models.description: Part of the seasonal 24 sekki series, its soft pink dial evokes cherry blossoms drifting on water in spring, in a case reinterpreting the 1967 62GS.

models.name: Kodo Constant-force Tourbillon
models.description: Grand Seiko's first haute horlogerie complication, combining a constant-force mechanism and tourbillon on a single axis in an openworked limited edition of 20.

name: Credor
tagline: Seiko's hand-finished haute horlogerie in gold, platinum and porcelain
summary: Credor is Seiko's most exclusive brand, dedicated to precious-metal watches and artisanal finishing. Its Micro Artist Studio creates the cult Eichi II, while the Gérald Genta-designed Locomotive returned in 2024 as a titanium luxury sports watch.
history:
Credor began in 1974 as a high-end line of Seiko's precious-metal watches; the name combines the French 'crête d'or', or 'crest of gold'. It became a stand-alone brand in 1979. Through the 1970s and 80s Credor produced gold dress watches and, in 1979, the Locomotive, a sports watch designed by Gérald Genta with hexagonal screws and an integrated bracelet.

In 2000 Seiko established the Micro Artist Studio at its Shiojiri facility in Nagano, a small team of craftsmen led by Yoshifusa Nakazawa. It created some of Japan's most ambitious watches, including the Spring Drive Sonnerie (2006), the Spring Drive Minute Repeater (2011) and the Fugaku tourbillon (2016). Its best-known creation is the Eichi, a simple time-only watch with a porcelain dial, hand-painted indices and a hand-finished manually wound Spring Drive movement; the Eichi II followed in 2014 and is made in tiny numbers.

For its 50th anniversary in 2024, Credor revived the Locomotive in high-intensity titanium with a new in-house automatic, the CR01. Regular-production green and blue versions followed. Credor also makes the ultra-thin Goldfeather line, descended from Seiko's 1960 Goldfeather and the 1969 U.T.D.
knownFor: The Eichi II and the Gérald Genta-designed Locomotive
innovations: 2006: Spring Drive Sonnerie by the Micro Artist Studio
2011: Spring Drive Minute Repeater
2016: Fugaku tourbillon
2024: Cal. CR01 automatic for the revived Locomotive

models.name: Eichi II
models.description: A cult connoisseur's watch from the Micro Artist Studio: a pure white porcelain dial with hand-painted blue indices and an exquisitely hand-finished Spring Drive movement.

models.name: Locomotive

models.name: Goldfeather U.T.D.
models.description: An ultra-thin gold dress watch just 7.7 mm thick, continuing the lineage of Seiko's 1960 Goldfeather and 1969 U.T.D.

name: King Seiko
tagline: Seiko's 1960s high-grade rival to Grand Seiko, revived for a new era
summary: King Seiko was the high-grade line of Seiko's Daini Seikosha factory, built to compete with Suwa's Grand Seiko in the 1960s. Revived in 2022, it now offers faceted, sharply finished mechanical watches between Seiko Presage and Grand Seiko.
history:
King Seiko was introduced in 1961 by Daini Seikosha, the Tokyo-area Seiko factory that competed internally with Suwa Seikosha, maker of Grand Seiko. The rivalry pushed both teams to improve accuracy and finishing, and King Seiko quickly earned a reputation for crisp, faceted cases and reliable movements.

The 1965 KSK introduced a hacking seconds function, protected crown and the distinctive shield logo, and its sharp lugs and flat surfaces became a design hallmark. Later models, including the 45KCM of 1969 and the 5626 and 56KS automatics, featured high-beat and chronometer-grade movements. The line was wound down in the mid-1970s as quartz transformed Seiko's business.

In 2021 Seiko released a limited recreation of the KSK, and in 2022 King Seiko returned as a full collection. The range has since grown to include the KSK series, the KS1969 series based on the curved 45KCM, and in 2024 the angular VANAC series inspired by a 1972 design, using the upgraded 6L35 and 8L45 movements.

Today King Seiko sits between Seiko Presage and Grand Seiko, with most models priced around $3,100 to $3,850. Its cases emphasise flat, sharply faceted surfaces and wide polished bevels, echoing the internal rivalry that once pushed Daini Seikosha and Suwa Seikosha to outdo each other.
knownFor: Faceted 1960s cases and the KSK shield
innovations: 1965: KSK adds hacking seconds and a crown guard to the line
1968: Chronometer-grade King Seiko models with high-beat movements

timeline.event: First King Seiko launched by Daini Seikosha

models.name: KS1969
models.description: Based on the 1969 45KCM, with a distinctive curved case silhouette and a silver dial.

models.name: VANAC

name: Citizen
tagline: Light-powered Eco-Drive pioneer and one of the world's largest watchmakers
summary: Citizen is one of the world's largest watch manufacturers and the name behind Eco-Drive, light-powered quartz that never needs a battery change. Vertically integrated and technically ambitious, it also owns Bulova, Frédérique Constant, Alpina, Arnold & Son and the movement maker Miyota.
history:
Citizen's story begins in 1918 with the Shokosha Watch Research Institute in Tokyo, founded by jeweller Kamekichi Yamazaki to build a domestic watch industry. In 1924 it produced a pocket watch named 'Citizen' by Tokyo mayor Shinpei Goto, who hoped it would be a watch loved by ordinary citizens. Citizen Watch Co. was established in 1930 with the help of Swiss-born investor Rodolphe Schmid.

After the war Citizen grew rapidly, pioneering shock resistance and water resistance for the domestic market and, in 1970, the X-8 Chronometer, the world's first watch with a titanium case. In 1976 it launched the Crystron Solar Cell, the first light-powered analog quartz watch, the technology that became Eco-Drive in 1995. It also made the world's first multi-band radio-controlled watch in 1993 and, in 2011, the first light-powered watch to set itself via GPS satellites.

Citizen expanded internationally by acquisition: Bulova in 2008, the Swiss movement maker La Joux-Perret in 2012, and Frédérique Constant, Alpina and Ateliers deMonaco in 2016. In 2019 it unveiled Caliber 0100, a light-powered quartz accurate to ±1 second per year.

Today Citizen Watch Co. is listed in Tokyo and headquartered in Nishitokyo. Watches are its largest business alongside machine tools and components, and core lines include Promaster, Tsuyosa, Series 8 and The Citizen.
knownFor: Eco-Drive light-powered watches and the Promaster line
innovations: 1970: X-8 Chronometer, the first watch with a titanium case
1976: Crystron Solar Cell, the first light-powered analog quartz watch
1993: First multi-band radio-controlled watch
2011: Eco-Drive Satellite Wave, first light-powered GPS-synchronized watch
2019: Caliber 0100, accurate to ±1 second per year

funFacts: The brand name was chosen by Tokyo's mayor, who wanted a watch for ordinary citizens.

Citizen also makes CNC machine tools under the Cincom and Miyano names.

models.name: Tsuyosa

models.name: Garrison

name: Casio
tagline: The digital watch icon: cheap, indestructible and everywhere
summary: Casio turned electronics expertise into the world's most ubiquitous digital watches. Its inexpensive resin and steel classics such as the F-91W, A168 and CA-53W calculator watch have sold in enormous numbers and become design icons, alongside higher lines such as Edifice, Pro Trek and G-Shock.
history:
Casio was founded in Tokyo in 1946 by engineer Tadao Kashio as Kashio Seisakujo, initially making parts and a finger ring that held a cigarette. Tadao and his brothers Toshio, Kazuo and Yukio went on to build the 14-A in 1957, the world's first compact all-electric calculator, and the company was incorporated as Casio Computer Co. that year.

Casio's expertise in integrated circuits led to its first watch, the Casiotron, in 1974, one of the earliest digital watches with an automatic calendar. Mass-produced LCD watches followed, with ever more functions: calculators, databanks, games and alarms. The rugged G-Shock arrived in 1983, and in 1989 Casio launched the F-91W, a simple resin digital watch that remains in production and has sold in the tens of millions.

Through the 1990s and 2000s Casio added Tough Solar power, Multi-Band radio-controlled timekeeping, the Pro Trek outdoor line and the Edifice motorsport line. The Timepiece segment is now Casio's largest business, with sales of about ¥166 billion in the year to March 2025, and G-Shock makes up roughly half of it.

The company remains headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, and the Kashio family still plays a leading role in management.

innovations: 1957: 14-A, the first compact all-electric calculator (pre-watch)
1974: Casiotron, a digital watch with a fully automatic calendar
1980: Calculator watches enter mass production
1983: G-Shock shock-resistant watch

name: G-Shock
tagline: The toughest watch ever made, born from a dropped watch in 1983
summary: G-Shock is Casio's shock-resistant watch brand and a global cultural phenomenon, spanning $100 resin squares to titanium MR-G pieces. Engineered around a floating module inside a hollow resin case, it has sold well over 100 million units and dominates street, military and outdoor culture.
history:
G-Shock began in 1981 when Casio engineer Kikuo Ibe dropped and broke a watch his father had given him. He proposed a watch that would survive a 10-metre drop, offer 10-bar water resistance and a 10-year battery, the 'Triple 10' concept. His small 'Project Team Tough' tested around 200 prototypes, famously dropping them from a third-floor bathroom window, before hitting on a module 'floating' inside a hollow, shock-absorbing structure.

The first G-Shock, the square DW-5000C, launched in April 1983. Sales were slow until an American TV ad showing a G-Shock being used as a hockey puck caught attention, and the brand was adopted by skaters, surfers, police and soldiers. Keanu Reeves wore a DW-5600 in the 1994 film Speed, and the 1990s brought the Frogman diver, the Mudman and collaborations with street and fashion labels.

Tough Solar and Multi-Band 6 radio timekeeping arrived in the 2000s, followed by Bluetooth. Casio reached 100 million cumulative G-Shock shipments in 2017. The octagonal GA-2100, nicknamed the 'CasiOak', became a 2019 sensation, and the full-metal GMW-B5000 and titanium MR-G lines took the square design upmarket.

G-Shock accounts for roughly half of Casio's timepiece sales and ships over a million and a half watches per quarter.
knownFor: Near-indestructible shock-resistant digital watches
innovations: 1983: Floating-module shock-resistant structure (DW-5000C)
1993: Frogman, the first ISO-rated G-Shock diver
2000s: Tough Solar and Multi-Band 6 radio control
2019: Carbon Core Guard structure in the thin GA-2100

name: Orient
tagline: In-house Japanese automatics at prices few can match
summary: Orient is a Japanese watchmaker, now part of Seiko Epson, famous for affordable mechanical watches with in-house movements. The Bambino dress watch and the Mako and Kamasu divers are some of the most recommended entry-level automatics in the world.
history:
Orient's roots go back to 1901, when Shogoro Yoshida opened the Yoshida Watch Shop in Tokyo's Ueno district, selling imported pocket watches. The business began manufacturing, and after the Second World War the factory in Hino, Tokyo was reorganized in 1950 as Tama Keiki Co. In 1951 it was renamed Orient Watch Co., and the same year it launched the Orient Star.

Through the 1950s to 70s Orient built a range of mechanical watches for the domestic and export markets, including the Royal Orient and the Orient King Diver. Unlike most Japanese makers, Orient stayed loyal to mechanical watches through the quartz era, which later became its main selling point abroad.

Orient had long cooperated with Seiko Epson, which became its majority owner and made it a subsidiary in 2009. In 2017 Orient Watch Co. was fully merged into Epson, and the brand is now run as Epson's watch business, with movements made at Epson's facilities in Akita and Nagano.

Today Orient is best known in export markets for its value-driven automatics: the domed-crystal Bambino, the Mako diver launched about two decades ago, and the sapphire-equipped Kamasu of 2019, all powered by in-house calibres.
knownFor: The Bambino dress watch and the Mako and Kamasu divers
innovations: 1951: Orient Star launched, the brand's high-grade line
2010s: In-house F6 automatic calibres with hacking and hand-winding at entry prices

name: Orient Star
tagline: Orient's high-grade 'Shining Star', famous for open-heart and power-reserve dials
summary: Orient Star is the premium line of Orient, created in 1951 to be the 'shining star' of mechanical watches. Now under Seiko Epson, it is known for semi-skeleton dials, power reserve indicators and the M42 Diver 1964 series.
history:
Orient Star was launched in 1951, the same year Tama Keiki was renamed Orient Watch Co. Its name expressed the ambition to create a watch that shines brightest among mechanical timepieces, and the first model was chronometer-grade. Through the 1950s and 60s the line represented Orient's best work, and in 1964 Orient made its first diver's watch, the design source for today's M42 Diver 1964 series.

When quartz swept Japan, Orient continued to invest in mechanical watches. In 1996 it released the first Orient Star with a power reserve indicator, which became the line's signature, followed by world time, GMT and, from the 2000s, the Semi Skeleton and Skeleton models that open up the dial to show the balance wheel.

Orient became a subsidiary of Seiko Epson in 2009 and merged fully into Epson in 2017. Since then Orient Star has been repositioned as a distinct brand with collections such as Classic, Contemporary, Sports and M-Line, using Epson's precision finishing and the F6 and F8 calibres.

In the current range, the Classic Semi Skeleton pairs an open window over the balance with the signature power reserve indicator, while the M42 Diver 1964 2nd Edition offers a 41 mm, 200 m diver with sapphire crystal and the F6N47 calibre. Orient Star is positioned as the more refined, better-finished sibling of the value-focused Orient line.

innovations: 1951: First Orient Star, chronometer-grade

name: Minase
tagline: Case-in-case construction and Sallaz polish from a village in snowy Akita
summary: Minase is a small Japanese luxury brand created by precision-tool and watch-case maker Kyowa in the mountains of Akita. It is known for its patented 'case in case' architecture, where the dial and movement float inside a sapphire-windowed outer shell, and for mirror-sharp Sallaz (Zaratsu) polishing.
history:
Minase's parent company, Kyowa Co., Ltd., was founded in 1963 as a maker of precision cutting drills in Akita Prefecture. From the 1960s it expanded into manufacturing watch cases for both mass-market and high-end watch brands, and by 1996 it had become a full watch manufacturer capable of design, development and production.

In 2005 Kyowa launched its own brand, named after the village of Minase where its workshop sits, a remote, snowy area the company likes to compare with Switzerland's Vallée de Joux. The first watches formed the Master Craft series. In 2011 it completed the HiZ series, which codified the brand's three signatures: Sallaz hand-polishing, the modular 'case in case' construction inspired by Japanese three-dimensional puzzles, and the MORE (Minase Original Rebuild Equation) concept, meant to make every part replaceable so a watch can last a century.

Collections such as the Divido, the architectural 7 Windows and the square Horizon use Swiss ETA 2892A2-based movements finished in-house, while the Mastercraft line features traditional Japanese crafts such as urushi lacquer. Minase makes fewer than 500 watches a year. Delivery typically takes around three months because of the limited, hand-finished production.
knownFor: Floating 'case in case' construction and Sallaz polishing
innovations: 2011: Patented 'case in case' construction introduced with the HiZ series
2011: MORE concept for fully rebuildable cases and bracelets
2017: Completion of an original Minase movement

name: Kurono Tokyo
tagline: Hajime Asaoka's accessible Art Deco watches that sell out in minutes
summary: Kurono Tokyo is the accessible brand of AHCI independent watchmaker Hajime Asaoka. It pairs his meticulous dial and case designs with reliable Japanese movements, released in small batches that routinely sell out almost instantly.
history:
Kurono Tokyo was launched in 2019 by Hajime Asaoka, the Tokyo designer-turned-watchmaker whose hand-built tourbillons had earned him AHCI membership but cost far more than most collectors could pay. The idea was to share the design DNA of his atelier watches, including hand-drawn typefaces, multi-layer dials, hand-mixed colours and carefully proportioned cases, at a fraction of the price by using off-the-shelf Japanese movements.

Early models were small-batch, mostly online releases that sold out quickly, building a devoted international following. The range has grown into several series: the Bunkyo Tokyo Classic series of Art Deco three-handers, the Grand series with urushi lacquer dials made by a master craftsman, a Complications series including the Chronograph I and II with Seiko column-wheel calibres and the Calendrier full calendar, and Special Projects such as 34 mm Art Deco and meteorite-dial editions.

Kurono now operates salons in Aoyama, Tokyo and in Shanghai, and in 2026 released its first diver's watch.

Typical releases illustrate the formula: the 34 mm Art Deco models of 2022 used a Miyota 90S5 and were limited to 80 pieces per colour, the Calendrier Type I combined a Miyota 9122 with a domed khaki dial and full calendar, and the Chronograph II used Seiko's NE86 column-wheel movement with a multi-layered lacquered dial.

2026: Two-in-one diver with a sealed outer diving case

name: Naoya Hida & Co.
tagline: Ultra-classical Japanese watches with hand-engraved dials made in tiny numbers
summary: Naoya Hida & Co. is a Tokyo independent making ultra-classical, Calatrava-inspired watches with hand-engraved German silver dials. Produced in runs of a handful to a few dozen pieces, they have become some of the most sought-after Japanese independent watches.
history:
Naoya Hida founded his company in Tokyo in 2018. Before that he had worked on the retail side of high-end watchmaking, representing brands including F.P. Journe, and he set out to make the purely classical watch he felt was missing: small steel cases, time-only or simple complications, and dials engraved by hand rather than printed.

In 2020 master watchmaker Kousuke Fujita, a Hiko Mizuno and WOSTEP graduate who had worked at Seiko and F.P. Journe, joined to handle movement work and assembly. The watches use heavily reworked Swiss movements, for example Valjoux 7750-family calibres stripped of their automatic and chronograph works and converted to manual winding, housed in 904L steel or gold cases. Dials are German silver with hand-engraved numerals filled with urushi lacquer, paired with heat-blued or solid gold hands.

The collection is organised by 'Type': the Type 1 series with small seconds, Type 2 with central seconds, Type 3 moon phases, the rectangular Type 5 of 2024, a perpetual calendar Type 6A in 2025 and, in 2026, its first chronograph using a vintage Valjoux 23-family movement. Each reference is made in very small numbers, usually 2 to 25 pieces, and allocations are heavily oversubscribed.

2025: NH Type 6A, the brand's first perpetual calendar

name: Otsuka Lotec
tagline: Industrial-machine aesthetics and jumping hours from a one-man Tokyo workshop
summary: Otsuka Lotec is the brand of Tokyo designer-watchmaker Jiro Katayama, who makes watches that look like pieces of vintage industrial equipment. His jumping-hour and retrograde displays, turret windows and meter-like dials have made the brand a cult favourite among independent collectors.
history:
Jiro Katayama, a product designer by training, began making watches around 2008 after buying a used bench lathe in an online auction. Working from a small workshop in Tokyo, he taught himself to machine cases and modules, drawing inspiration from the forms, textures and details of old industrial objects such as gauges, meters and machinery.

Otsuka Lotec began selling watches commercially in 2012. Its numbered models, such as No. 5, No. 6 and No. 7, combine Japanese Miyota base movements with Katayama's own complication modules: the No. 6 shows retrograde hours and minutes on a fan-shaped meter, while the No. 7 and No. 7.5 display a jumping hour through turret-shaped windows with rotating minute and second discs. Demand quickly outstripped his tiny output, and pieces became famous for being nearly impossible to buy.

In 2023 the core models were redesigned with upgraded materials. The brand has since expanded upward with the No. 9, a rectangular piece with an in-house manual movement combining jumping hours, rewinding minutes, a tourbillon and hour striking, and the No. 8 of 2026. Otsuka Lotec watches are displayed permanently at Isetan Shinjuku.

name: Hajime Asaoka
tagline: Japan's first independent tourbillon maker, designing and machining every part himself
summary: Hajime Asaoka is a Tokyo-based AHCI independent watchmaker who, in 2009, completed the first tourbillon wristwatch made by an independent in Japan. His small output of tourbillons, chronographs and time-only watches, with movements made in his own workshop, is among the most coveted in Japanese watchmaking.
history:
Hajime Asaoka was born in Kanagawa in 1965 and graduated in design from Tokyo University of the Arts. In 1992 he founded his own design office, working as a product designer and becoming an early expert in 3D computer graphics for advertising and magazines. A commission to design a watch led him to teach himself watchmaking, and he began making watches in 2005.

Working largely alone with CNC machines and hand tools, in 2009 he presented a high-end mechanical wristwatch with a tourbillon, the first made by an independent watchmaker in Japan. His striking designs, combining Art Deco typography with engineering precision, drew global attention, and he became a full member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI).

Asaoka's watches include the Tsunami, a time-only watch with an unusually large 15 mm balance; a classical column-wheel Chronograph; the Tourbillon Pura with an A7075 duralumin carriage; and Project T, a tourbillon developed with aerospace machinist Yuki Precision and tool maker OSG, which uses tiny ball bearings in place of some jewels. He makes all the movement parts in his own workshop, run as Precision Watch Tokyo. In 2019 he launched Kurono Tokyo to offer his designs at accessible prices. In 2024 his company also revived the defunct Nagoya brand Takano with the Chateau Nouvelle, the first Japanese watch certified by the Besançon Observatory.

name: Masahiro Kikuno
tagline: Hand-made Japanese temporal-hour watches and tourbillons, built without CNC
summary: Masahiro Kikuno is a Japanese independent watchmaker and AHCI member known for reinterpreting traditional Japanese timekeeping, above all the wadokei temporal-hour watch, whose hour markers move with the seasons. For years he made almost every part by hand without CNC machines.
history:
Masahiro Kikuno was born in 1983 in Hokkaido. He studied at the Hiko Mizuno College of Jewelry in Tokyo, completing its WOSTEP-linked watchmaking course between 2005 and 2008, and began building complicated watches entirely by hand, using manual lathes and files rather than computer-controlled machines.

His early works, a tourbillon and a perpetual calendar tourbillon, caught the attention of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI); he became a candidate in 2011 and a full member in 2013. In 2011 he also unveiled the Wadokei, a wristwatch rendering of the Japanese temporal-hour system, in which daytime and night-time are each divided into six units whose length changes through the year. Its hand-painted indices shift automatically, spreading out in summer daytime and contracting in winter.

Later pieces include Orizuru (2013), Mokume (2014) with a mokume-gane pattern, several unique 'Wadokei Revision' pieces, and Sakubou (2017), a moon phase in a kuro-shibuichi and white gold case accurate to one day in 122 years and made at only four pieces a year. In 2025 he presented Complication 'inherit', a minute repeater, chronograph and tourbillon inspired by George Daniels, and his first watch made with CNC assistance.

name: Knot
tagline: Made-in-Japan watches you build yourself from thousands of case and strap combinations
summary: Maker's Watch Knot is a Tokyo brand, founded in 2014, that sells affordable made-in-Japan watches designed to be mixed and matched with a huge range of straps. Its gallery shops let customers choose from over 100,000 combinations, and its Takumi line features traditional Japanese crafts on the dial.
history:
Knot was founded in 2014 in Kichijoji, Tokyo, with the aim of offering well-made Japanese watches at accessible prices while letting customers personalise them. Rather than selling finished watches, it separates cases and straps: buyers pick a watch head and then choose from around 200 straps made with its network of partner artisans, allowing more than 100,000 combinations.

The brand grew quickly through direct-to-consumer sales and its own gallery shops, now numbering a dozen across Japan. Its range spans quartz and solar watches, Miyota and Epson-powered automatics with sapphire crystals and Zaratsu-polished cases, and a premium Takumi collection featuring crafts such as Kanazawa gold leaf, urushi lacquer and raden mother-of-pearl inlay.

Knot also produces custom and corporate watches, with collaborations including Uniqlo, Studio Ghibli, Kyocera and the Yokohama DeNA BayStars.

The company, Knot Co., Ltd., is led by founder Hiromitsu Endo and began in a small apartment room in Kichijoji. Its Takumi collection works with named artisans: raden and urushi dials by lacquer craftsman Nobuichi Ohtake, and Kanazawa gold-leaf dials made with Hakuichi, a gold-leaf company founded in 1975 in a craft tradition more than 400 years old. Strap partners include makers of Tochigi leather.

name: Sea-Gull (Tianjin Seagull)
tagline: China's pioneering movement maker, from the 1963 air force chronograph to tourbillons
summary: Tianjin Seagull is China's oldest and most important mechanical watchmaker and one of the world's largest producers of mechanical movements. Famous for the 1963 aviation chronograph reissue, it also makes tourbillons, minute repeaters and other high complications at comparatively low prices.
history:
Seagull began in January 1955 as the state-run Tianjin Watch Factory, started by four craftsmen, and that year produced the Wuxing (Five Star), considered China's first domestically made mechanical wristwatch. In 1963 the factory developed the D304, a manually wound chronograph built for the Chinese Air Force and regarded as China's first aviation chronograph.

Through the planned-economy decades the factory produced millions of watches and the Chinese standard movement. It gained national company status in 1990 and in 1992 became Tianjin Seagull Corporation. After a brief push into quartz, it returned to mechanical watchmaking exclusively in 1997, and it listed on the stock market in 2000. Its movements, including the ST19 chronograph calibre descended from Swiss Venus tooling, have been used by many brands worldwide.

Seagull has since moved into haute horlogerie, presenting the ST9250 in 2009, combining a tourbillon, minute repeater and perpetual calendar, and developing multi-axis and ultra-thin tourbillons. In 2010 it moved to new facilities near Tianjin airport. The 1963 chronograph, reissued in modern form and updated in 2023 for its 60th anniversary, remains its best-known watch abroad, and in 2025 it launched a global direct-to-consumer website.

name: Fiyta
tagline: China's space watch, worn on Shenzhou missions since 2003
summary: FIYTA is a Shenzhen watchmaker controlled by the state aerospace group AVIC and best known for supplying the watches used on China's crewed Shenzhou space missions. It is one of China's largest watch brands and also runs a major watch retail network.
history:
FIYTA was established in Shenzhen in 1987, growing out of the aviation industry's move into precision consumer products. It became one of the leading domestic watch brands during China's economic opening, and its parent company, FIYTA Precision Technology, is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange with the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) as its controlling shareholder.

The brand's defining moment came on 15 October 2003, when a FIYTA space watch accompanied Yang Liwei, China's first astronaut, on Shenzhou 5; the watch was used to time spacesuit leak checks. FIYTA has since supplied watches for subsequent crewed missions, developing a manual-wound mechanical space movement with AM/PM display and timing functions, and markets its record of zero functional failures in space.

In 2011 FIYTA became the first Chinese watch brand invited to exhibit in Hall 1 at Baselworld. It pioneered titanium and carbon-fibre cases in China from 2007, and in 2016 it reportedly took control of the historic Beijing Watch Factory. Today its range covers the Space collection (Mars-500, Space Shuttle, Spacewalk), elegant women's watches, and classic and diver lines, alongside its Harmony watch retail business.

name: Beijing Watch Factory
tagline: China's capital-city watchmaker, specialists in hand-finished tourbillons
summary: Beijing Watch Factory, founded in 1958, is one of China's historic watchmakers and today concentrates on high-end mechanical watches, especially tourbillons with traditional Chinese decoration. It produces movements, components and complete watches.
history:
Beijing Watch Factory (Beijing Shoubiao Chang) was established in 1958, during the period when China set up state watch factories to make the country self-sufficient in timepieces, and its early watches were sold under the 'Beijing' name. Over the following decades it produced mechanical watches for the domestic market, including the Shuangling (Double Rhombus) line, which became a well-known Chinese watch name.

As the market liberalised and cheap quartz arrived, the factory reoriented toward high-end mechanical watchmaking. It developed its own movements and became known for tourbillons and elaborate hand decoration such as engraving and skeletonisation drawing on Chinese artistic themes, positioning itself as a Chinese counterpart to Swiss haute horlogerie.

The company later became privately owned and employed around 600 people in 2013. According to published sources, the Shenzhen watch group FIYTA acquired it in 2016. Detailed current model and pricing information is limited outside China. Its product range spans complete watches, in-house movements and components, and the factory presents its top tourbillon pieces as showcases of Chinese high watchmaking.

name: Atelier Wen
tagline: A 'Chinese soul' in guilloché, enamel and tantalum, from a Sino-French duo
summary: Atelier Wen is a Sino-French brand creating high-end watches that celebrate Chinese craftsmanship, notably hand-turned guilloché dials by master Cheng Yucai and grand feu enamel. Its integrated-bracelet Perception has become one of the most acclaimed new watches to come out of China.
history:
Atelier Wen was founded in 2018 by two Frenchmen, Robin Tallendier and Wilfried Buiron, who met while studying in Beijing in 2016 and were frustrated by the dismissive way Chinese craftsmanship was often seen. Their aim was to make 'a high quality timepiece with a Chinese soul'. Their first Kickstarter campaign in October 2018, for the Porcelain Odyssey Hao and Ji models with porcelain dials, was funded in under 30 minutes.

After a pause to refine the concept, the brand relaunched in 2022 with the Perception, an integrated-bracelet steel sports watch with hand-turned guilloché dials by Cheng Yucai, described as China's first master of the craft, and a Chinese Dandong movement. It sold out in 16 hours. Collaborations with Wristcheck and a titanium Millésime followed.

The brand has since moved upmarket. In 2025 it launched the Ancestra dress watch with a grand feu enamel dial and the Inflection, a full-tantalum integrated watch with enamel dials by Kong Lingjun's workshop and a customised Girard-Perregaux movement. In 2026 the Perception V3 adopted a French Pequignet EPM03 chronometer-grade movement. Atelier Wen coordinates design and production from Beijing and has its office in Hong Kong.

name: Titan
tagline: India's watch giant, from mass-market quartz to ultra-thin Edge mechanicals
summary: Titan is India's largest watchmaker and one of the world's biggest by volume, a Tata Group company that sells about 15 million watches a year across brands including Titan, Sonata and Fastrack. Its Edge line is known for ultra-thin design, and it has recently built in-house mechanical and tourbillon movements.
history:
Titan was founded on 26 July 1984 by Xerxes Desai as Titan Watches Limited, a joint venture between the Tata Group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO). A factory for quartz analogue watches was built in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, inaugurated by J.R.D. Tata, and the Titan brand launched in 1987, transforming an Indian market until then dominated by the state-owned HMT.

Titan grew quickly with design-led quartz watches and added brands for every segment: Sonata for value, Fastrack for youth (spun off as an independent brand in 2005), Raga for women and Nebula in solid gold. In 2002 it launched the Edge, a quartz watch that was among the thinnest in the world. It diversified into jewellery with Tanishq in 1994 and eyewear, and jewellery now makes up most of Titan Company's revenue. In 2011 Titan bought the Swiss brand Favre-Leuba.

Titan runs several manufacturing sites making cases, quartz and mechanical movements. It developed a 12-line 4 Hz mechanical calibre in 2015, India's first tourbillon movement in 2024 for the limited Jalsa Tourbillon, and in 2026 the Edge UltraSlim Mechanical with a 2.2 mm hand-wound calibre.

name: HMT
tagline: 'Timekeepers to the Nation': India's state watchmaker behind the Janata
summary: HMT, the watch division of state-owned Hindustan Machine Tools, made India's first mass-produced wristwatches from 1961 and dominated the market for decades. Its hand-wound Janata and Pilot are nostalgic icons, and HMT Limited still sells watches online.
history:
HMT, Hindustan Machine Tools, set up a watch factory in Bangalore in 1961 in collaboration with Japan's Citizen Watch. Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru released the first wristwatches made there, and HMT quickly became the watch of a newly independent India, sold with the slogan 'Timekeepers to the Nation'.

Its hand-wound mechanical watches, above all the Janata ('people's') and the Pilot, were affordable, durable and ubiquitous; other lines included the Jhalak semi-skeleton, Sona, Sujata, Rajat and a Braille watch. Production expanded to new factories at Tumkur (1978) and Ranibagh (1985), HMT began making quartz analogue watches in 1981, and it also built floral, tower and solar clocks, including the famous floral clock at Lalbagh in Bangalore.

From the late 1980s, competition from Titan and liberalisation eroded HMT's position, and slow decision-making kept it from modernising. HMT Watches Ltd. was closed in 2016, triggering a rush for the remaining stock among collectors. The brand did not disappear: HMT Limited's auxiliary business division in Jalahalli, Bengaluru, continues to sell HMT-branded mechanical, automatic, quartz, skeleton and Braille watches, including Janata, Pilot and Jawan automatics, through its official online shop.

name: Undone
tagline: Hong Kong's custom-made watches: design your own for a few hundred dollars
summary: Undone is a Hong Kong brand that lets customers customise affordable mechanical and mecha-quartz watches online, from dials and hands to cases and straps. It is known for vintage-inspired chronographs, the Basecamp field watch and a long list of pop-culture collaborations.
history:
Undone was founded in Hong Kong in 2014 by Michael Young, who had previously restored vintage Rolex watches and believed that true luxury meant a product made for its owner. The brand launched with 'accessible bespoke' watches: customers choose case, dial, hands, crown and strap in an online configurator, and the watch is assembled to order.

Unlike many microbrands, Undone keeps most operations in-house, including design, R&D, component manufacture and assembly, outsourcing only crystals and movements, typically Japanese Seiko/TMI NH35A automatics and mecha-quartz chronograph movements. Early hits included the Urban vintage chronographs, inspired by 1960s and 70s racing chronographs, the Aqua diver and the Basecamp tool watch with California dial options.

The brand has built a strong following through collaborations with Hello Kitty, Sanrio, Ghost in the Shell, hololive, POPEYE, the Manta Trust and the Atlassian Williams F1 team. Its range now includes the Aquadeep titanium diver, Terra, ultra-thin 4.9 mm Slim and enamel automatics. Early Basecamp models came on Cordura NATO straps, and buyers can add initials to the dial or caseback for a small fee. Watches typically sell for about $265 to $1,150.

name: Memorigin
tagline: Hong Kong's tourbillon-only brand, mixing Chinese culture and pop-culture tie-ins
summary: Memorigin is a Hong Kong brand founded in 2011 that makes only tourbillon watches, at prices far below Swiss equivalents. It combines Chinese artistic motifs with a long list of licensed collaborations, from Star Wars and Marvel to Bruce Lee and Kamen Rider.
history:
Memorigin (Chinese name 萬希泉, 'a fountain of hopes for the masses') was founded in Hong Kong in 2011 by William Shum, who started the business after completing a master's degree at Cornell University. Drawing on his family's appreciation of Chinese woodcarving, he set out to create Hong Kong's first tourbillon watch brand, making the complication accessible and designing pieces as heirlooms to be passed from father to son.

Memorigin's watches all feature tourbillons, many of them flying tourbillons in openworked dials, with cultural themes such as dragons, the Chinese zodiac and traditional instruments. The brand became widely known through licensed collaborations with Warner Bros. (Batman), Disney (Marvel's Avengers and Star Wars), the Bruce Lee Foundation (2018), Kamen Rider and, in 2026, Stephen Chow's Kung Fu Soccer, plus athletes including Michael Owen and LaMelo Ball.

Its current collections are grouped into Cultural, Timeless, Glamorous and Seamless series, and the brand also offers bespoke tourbillon commissions. Movement materials are sourced from Europe, and the brand says pieces undergo international testing before release. Designs range from classical pieces such as the Eternal Blue, with a silver clous de Paris dial, blue Roman numerals and an 80-hour reserve, to openworked cushion-shaped and luminous carbon-fibre models.

name: Ciga Design
tagline: The Chinese design studio whose rotating-Earth Blue Planet won at the GPHG
summary: CIGA Design is a Shenzhen watch brand founded by industrial designer Zhang Jianmin that focuses on bold, design-led mechanical watches at accessible prices. Its Blue Planet, which tells time with a rotating 3D Earth, won the GPHG Challenge Watch Prize in 2021.
history:
CIGA Design was founded in 2016 by Zhang Jianmin, an industrial designer who previously created wayfinding and guidance systems for public spaces such as airports and railway stations. Rather than a traditional watch factory, CIGA operates as a design studio with an international team, assembling its watches in China with movements sourced from China, Japan and Switzerland.

The brand made its name with the Series Z 'Edge' and other skeleton designs, winning numerous design awards including iF, Red Dot and a German Design Award 2020, and set crowdfunding records on Indiegogo. Its breakthrough came in 2021 when the Blue Planet, which replaces conventional hands with a CNC-engraved topographic Earth that rotates beneath a fixed pointer, won the Challenge Watch Prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève, reported as the first GPHG prize for a Chinese mechanical watch.

CIGA has since developed its own calibres, including the CD-04-E automatic for the Blue Planet and, from 2023, an in-house central tourbillon used in the Everest series. It says its watches are available in over 100 countries and have more than 500,000 users.
